questions.question: Explain why a government might intervene in a market in which a good is produced with an external cost. (4 marks)

A specific tax of $15 a tonne is imposed on Osira coal. The price buyers pay rises from $60 to $70 and the quantity traded falls from 60 to 50 tonnes a day. Calculate the consumer incidence of the tax and the revenue the government collects. (4 marks)
Draw a diagram to show the effect of a specific indirect tax of $15 a tonne on a market in which production generates an external cost of $15 a tonne. (4 marks)
Draw a diagram to show the effect of a subsidy of $12 a consultation on a market in which consumption generates an external benefit of $12 a consultation. (4 marks)

In Osira flats the market rent is $500 a month. A maximum price of $400 is imposed, at which quantity demanded is 250 flats and quantity supplied is 150. Calculate the excess demand created. (2 marks)
Analyse the effects of a guaranteed minimum price on producers and consumers in an agricultural market. (6 marks)
Examine whether a government should use an indirect tax or a system of tradeable pollution permits to reduce emissions from an industry. (8 marks)
Explain how the provision of information by a government can increase the quantity consumed of a good that generates external benefits. (4 marks)
Discuss whether a government facing high fuel prices should subsidise fuel or use the money in some other way. (14 marks)
Evaluate the view that government intervention to correct market failure inevitably leads to government failure. (20 marks)

leaves.wording: The purpose of government intervention, including reference to market failure.
